As someone that built a computer with an A10-5800K APU, I never had an issue with it until recently with IOMMU and Gigabyte motherboards with Kernel 4.2+ under Arch, both with Catalyst and radeon drivers. If you don't mind not being able to play some more graphically intensive games and want to save money, go with an APU.

You have two choices, the fglrx driver, which is the one officially provided by AMD. It has some issues some times, but it's the fastest one. Or, you can use the open source radeon driver, which is almost entirely open source. However, as far as software is concerned, your GPU is the same whether it's packaged with the CPU or if it's a separate card. I actually run an Athlon 5350 as a HTPC and server (for things like owncloud). It's a good little chip, if you are feeling even more adventurous, you can turn it into a router.

I would also suggest a motherboard that uses the laptop power adapter. I have a kill-a-watt and it pulls around 20w idle and 40w under load, so leaving it running 24/7 is very cheap provided you have decent electric rates.

What do you plan to use it for? Music, movies, etc? APU will work great, I was running an A4 (maybe an A6, can't recall), and for that purpose it was fine. For gaming, I would strongly suggest a CPU and a GPU - but the athlon you linked, I would recommend something newer - you can get something FAR newer and still stay under $100 on the cpu, and you wouldn't have to pay much more for your motherboard - but the athlon will work. All depends on your usage. If it will be a primarily internet device, it will work.
